claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 18 and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me ask you a few questions about Alex to determine his eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he attending college, sixth form, or an approved training course?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's studying for his A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. 

**Are you currently living in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you.

**Does Alex currently work, and if so, how many hours per week does he work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work. He's focused on his studies at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure about that, to be honest. I don't think so, but I'm not entirely certain.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's okay. Let me ask a couple more questions to complete the assessment.

**Does Alex live with you full-time, or does he live with someone else for any period of time?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with me full-time at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions:

**Are you currently responsible for Alex - meaning you provide for his needs such as food, clothes, and accommodation?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I provide everything for him - his food, clothes, accommodation, all of that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for all that information.

One final question: **Do you or your partner (if you have one) have an individual income over £60,000 per year?** 

(This won't affect whether you're eligible for Child Benefit, but it may mean you need to pay a tax charge if you claim it.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, neither of us earns that much.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

- Alex is 18 years old and studying for his A-levels, which counts as approved education
- The rules allow Child Benefit for children under 20 who stay in approved education or training
- You live in the UK with Alex and are responsible for his care
- Alex doesn't work 24 hours or more per week (which would affect eligibility)
- You provide for all his needs including food, clothes, and accommodation

Since neither you nor your partner earns over £60,000, you also won't have to worry about the High Income Child Benefit tax charge.

If you haven't already claimed Child Benefit for Alex, you can apply through HMRC. If you're already receiving it, you should continue to be eligible as long as Alex remains in approved education or training (up until he turns 20).

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
